title: Pantheon PersonaMemory
description: Persona-specific memory object. Accumulates knowledge, preferences, and behavioural observations that are private to a single persona. Written by the persona-memory-svc; readable by the owning persona's sessions and authorised research/consultation sessions.

memory_id.description: Immutable unique identifier for this memory entry (UUID).

persona_id.description: The persona this memory belongs to. Scopes all read/write access.

memory_type.description:
Classification of what kind of knowledge this memory encodes.
- episodic: a specific past event or trade outcome
- semantic: a durable fact or pattern learned over time
- preference: operator-confirmed tuning of persona behaviour
- strategy_lesson: a lesson distilled from a research or postmortem review
- risk_observation: an observed risk pattern or regime flag
- consultation_outcome: a synthesised insight from a committee/consult session

structured_payload.description: Optional machine-readable payload whose shape is memory_type-dependent.

tags.description: Free-form retrieval tags (e.g. regime, asset_class, source_strategy).

source_event_type.description: The class of event that triggered the write-back.

source_event_id.description: ID of the specific source event (e.g. postmortem_id, session_id, evolution_decision_id).

written_at.description: Timestamp when this entry was written (UTC ISO-8601).

write_authority.description: Service that wrote this entry. Only whitelisted services may write.

embedding_ref.description: Reference to the vector embedding stored in the retrieval index. Set by persona-memory-svc after indexing.

superseded_by.description: memory_id of the entry that supersedes this one, if any. Superseded entries are retained for lineage but excluded from active retrieval.

relevance_scope.description: Controls read visibility. persona_private: only the owning persona's sessions. persona_and_committee: also readable by authorised committee/consult sessions involving this persona.

reuse_count.description: Incremented by the retrieval facade when this memory is reused in an authorized context.
